findings.message: The shader reads uTime, but the project has no app.onFrame together with a .runtime({ mutable: true }) node, so nothing drives time and uTime stays at its initial value.
findings.cause: The engine binds `uTime` from the host-supplied clock, which stays 0 unless you drive it, so a uTime-only animation is a frozen frame. This is a static guess; MOTION_NONE confirms it on a real frame.
findings.fix: Declare your own uniform (e.g. `waveClock`), mark the node `.runtime({ id: "water", mutable: true })`, and in `app.onFrame` call `app.nodes.require("water").setUniform?.("waveClock", seconds)`.

findings.message: Scene has no interactions. Suggested fix: add interactions.orbit() for product/viewer scenes.
findings.cause: The engine notes that the scene has no camera interaction. Fine for a fixed shot.
findings.fix: Add `interactions.orbit()` if a viewer should be able to move the camera.

findings.message: Two frames 1000 ms apart are identical (0.000% of pixels changed).
findings.cause: Two frames captured about a second apart are pixel-identical. Fine for a static product shot; a bug for water, particles or a game.
findings.fix: If the scene should animate, drive time yourself (`setUniform` in `app.onFrame` on a `.runtime({ mutable: true })` node) and check LINT_UTIME_NOT_ANIMATED.
